newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spot Products - Stock data depress late diffs.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spot Products - Stock data depress late diffs.

text.p: U.S. Gulf and New York Harbor product differentials narrowed across the board on new stock late Wednesday, players said, although Midwest Group Thrree values improved on continued shipment delays by the Explorer Pipeline.
Absolute values were also depressed by NYMEX action, with June gasoline settling 0.38 cent lower at 64.36 cents a gallon and June heating oil easing slightly to 56.42 cents.
The American Petroleum Institute data released Tuesday showed a build in gasoline stocks of 6.5 million barrels, well above market expectations, with daily refinery output of 8.1 million barrels.
- NEW YORK HARBOR

++ GASOLINE: Conventional M2 gasoline was traded late day for 1.75 cents below June futures, 0.25 cent weaker than Tuesday. "You have to blame the APIs," one East Coast player said, who noted trade was light as many traders attended an industry outing in upstate New York.
And prompt reformulated A2 gasoline eased 0.25 cent to offers of 1.25 cents, giving up ground after holding stable most of the day.
++ DISTILLATE: Market players quoted prompt heating oil barrels at about 0.10 cent under June NYMEX, about 0.40 cent weaker than Tuesday diffs.
And low sulfur diesel diffs narrowed 0.25 cent, with bids at 0.70 cent over the June print, depressed by API data showing a 761,000 barrel build in the East Coast during the week ending May 9.
- U.S. GULF
++ GASOLINE: Differentials eased throughout the day, with conventional unleaded offered at 4.25 cents below the June screen late day -- about 0.40 cent weaker than diffs seen late Tuesday.

++ DISTILLATE: Amples supplies drove differentials lower, with prompt heating oil talked near 2.50 cents under the June NYMEX, 0.45 cent weaker than Tuesday diffs. And prompt low sulphur diesel sold for 1.75 cents off the June NYMEX, 0.25 cent weaker.
"There's a lot of oil down here," said one trader, referring to the softer distillate values.
- MIDCONTINENT

++ GASOLINE: Prompt Group Three unleaded differentials soared more than 1.75 cents for the day, to 7.25 cents over June NYMEX gasoline as delays on the Explorer Pipeline pressured the front end higher.
In the afternoon, prompt delivery deals were done at 7.00 cents over the screen, pushing higher deliveries for May 20 and beyond.
Delivery by May 20th was pegged at about 5.50 cents, with May 30th at 3.25 cents.
"I think we may be seeing the any month coming up higher. It's all a timing thing," said a Houston player.
Explorer has said shipments on the 14th cycle have been delayed by about five to ten days. This means less material being stored in the Williams Pipeline system, which feeds the Midwest.
DISTILLATES: The Explorer delay also pressured Group Three low sulphur, whose diffs widened one cent to between 6.75 cents and 7.00 cents over the screen.
The Chicago cash markets were relatively steady, with conventional unleaded prompt differentials holding at about 2.50 cents over the screen.
- (( New York Energy Desk, 212 859-1620))
